Thank you very much for the feedback on what to change.
Please inform me if anything else needs to be fixed.
It seems to me like it would be a slight challenge to try to figure out the pattern to code based on tests provided. but I changed it.

Formatting / presentation
* Please study the formatting syntax described on this page: https://www.codingame.com/playgrounds/40701/help-center/statement , and format the statement properly by following the example there:

[[ ]] for variables (begin, n, k, r)
{{ }} for constants (1)
<< >> for bold (Line 1, Line 2, Line 3, Line 4)

General
* The Goal and Output sections specify that the output consists of one line only: the final value of [[begin]]. This is inconsistent with your solution and the expected output of the cases.

Constraints / Cases
* begin, n and k are never negative in the current cases. Please change -100 to 0, or modify the cases to cover the full range of possible values in a balanced manner.

* Similarly, n and k never exceed 10 in the current cases. Adjust the bound or modify the cases accordingly.

* Please increase the lower bound of r to 1.

* In general, please use a greater variety of input values. For example, r = 4 in half of the existing cases. That should be changed.

Stub generator
* Please change "beginn" to "begin".

Game modes
* It seems impossible to infer the task from visible cases only in Reverse mode. Consider disabling that mode.

Thanks.

Thank you for the quick follow-up.

Input
* Please remove the line above Line 1.

Output
* Please add "of [[begin]]" after "value".

Constraints
* Please format "begin", "n", "k" and "r" as [[variables]].

Cases
* Please remove the trailing newlines from these cases:
  • Validator 1 (input and output)
  • Test 2 (output)
  • Validator 2 (output)
  • Test 3 (input)

* Validator 4: The value of [[begin]] violates the first constraint. Please change it to another value not used in other cases.

Thanks again.

P.S. It'd be helpful to reply directly within the existing comment threads rather than creating new comments, so that others are notified of your responses.
Thank you so much for pointing those out to me. if you see any other issues please inform me as soon as possible.

You're welcome. I don't see anything else that needs attention for now. If I happen to notice anything further, I'll be happy to let you know. Of course, we're all contributing as volunteers, so we'll do our best whenever time allows.
do I put it out of work in progress? or wait.
You could wait for feedback from the other reviewers first, then take it out of WIP once you feel it's ready.
Understood. it says there are 19 views. what does that mean?
The 19 views represent the total number of times the page has been loaded. Each time the page is opened or refreshed, it counts as one view, even if it's the same person viewing it multiple times.

Understood. I'm curious what normally makes a good reverse game?
I was hoping this would be one, but it will work the way it is.

This is subjective, but in my view, a good reverse game should have the following characteristics:

1. The underlying task is inferable from visible test cases.

2. There shouldn't be multiple plausible ways to understand the task that could lead to different valid solutions.

3. Earlier test cases should generally be less obvious and require more thought to decipher. Later test cases can provide more hints or reveal additional patterns to help participants narrow down the intended solution.

4. The challenge shouldn't boil down to guessing a mathematical relationship between the inputs and outputs. It should incorporate meaningful programming elements, such as conditionals and string manipulation.

I was never able to understand any of the reverse games I played, but that info will come in handy if I decide to make one. 
Once again I thank you.
